newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Mar 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Mar 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said he believed three readings of at least 13 laws should be completed by the provisional legislature before the handover, including the one outlawing secessionary activities.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- Sources said Beijing had instructed that the director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, should not retire until after the handover of Macau in 1999 to support Tung and help with work related to the return of the Portuguese-run enclave. But Zhou Nan, director of the Hong Kong branch of Xinhua news agency -- China's de facto mission in the territory -- had been told to retire soon after the handover as the branch will function solely as a news agency after July 1.
-- APPLE DAILY -- A recent poll showed that colonial Governor Chris Patten's popularity remained higher than Tung's.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Sources said Tung would go to Beijing later this month, bringing along several senior civil servants to take part in activities celebrating the handover.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- China's Foreign Ministry attacked a bill passed by the U.S. Congress to monitor Beijing's implementation of the "one country two systems" principle after the handover, saying Washington was trying to interfere in China's internal affairs.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Hong Kong Monetary Authority chief executive Joseph Yam issued a stark reminder to the European Union of the power of Asian nations to destabilise their markets if the planned single European currency proved too risky.
-- Fashion retailer Giordano International added five mainland shareholders to its register by placing 40 million new shares to raise HK$196 million.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Sir Colin Marshall, president of the Confederation of British Industry, said British businesspeople's confidence in Hong Kong was on the rebound.
